brief: JPMorgan Market Intelligence moves to a Tactically Cautious / Neutral stance. Fundamentals stay intact, but six variables argue for a choppy 2 to 3 weeks: Warsh's remarks make the September 16 meeting live, positioning gives no clean directional read, post-Labor Day issuance widens credit spreads, September is the SPX's worst month, Momentum is down 21% to 34% from June highs, and AVGO's strong guide failed to lift the stock. Because Warsh judges the US at full employment, CPI on September 11 outranks Friday's NFP, and NFP sits in a good-news-is-bad-news regime: a strong print lifts yields and weighs on equities, while another negative print reignites stagflation concerns. Goldilocks is 30k to 70k. Feroli forecasts 50k versus the Street's 55k, prior -23k, unemployment unchanged at 4.1%. Market-implied hike odds are ~64%. The desk therefore recommends reducing net-longs toward a dollar-neutral or market-neutral approach: long NDX versus short RTY, Mag7 and Software over AI/Memory/Semis, Large-Cap Banks, Healthcare into midterms, short Credit ETFs and long VIX as hedges. Positioning Intelligence reports August as a further reset with US positioning back to neutral.
